sentences.text: Leave granted.
2. Heard Mr. Ravi Bakshi, learned counsel appearing for the appellant (Insurance Company).
The respondent Nos. 1 to 4 (claimants), are represented by Ms. Chandni Gubbi, learned counsel.
3. The claim here arise out of the death of Ramesh Kumar, who died in a road accident on 31.03.2014.
On that date, the car driven by the victim was hit by a tempo, driven by the owner-cum- driver (respondent No. 5).

The legal heirs of the deceased (Ramesh Kumar) claimed Rs.5 crore compensation before the MACT at Bengaluru under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act by projecting that the victim at the relevant time, was employed as a Deputy General Manager (Production), in Micro-Labs Limited, Bangalore.
4. In support of the claim, the claimants have produced the appointment letter, the salary certificates and bank balance.
The victims employment status is also founded on the evidence of the Senior Vice President, Human Resources at Micro-Labs Limited, who deposed as witness (PW-3).

The relevant documents were produced by the employers witness and were accordingly exhibited.
5. Reason:
The learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the victims income was pegged on the higher side.
It is also argued that only 40% is to be added towards future prospect but here the learned Tribunal had added 50% of the assessed income toward future prospects.

sentences.text: It is also contended that ex post facto e-income tax return, should not be made the basis for computing the income of the deceased.

Such submission is otherwise valid but in the present case,
the claimants have also produced other documents like appointment letter, pay slips and bank account details proved by PW-3 for indicating the victims income.
7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimants would argue that while the MACT had awarded interest @ 8% p.a., the High Court had reduced the interest to @ 6% p.a. only.

8. The net salary after deduction of income tax and professional tax for the deceased in the present case supported by the relevant documents as mentioned above would work out to Rs.12,43,877.60 (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty Three Thousand Eight Hundred and Seventy Seven and Sixty paisa))
only per annum.

If Rs.3,10,969.40 (Rupees Three Lakhs Ten Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty Nine and Forty paisa) only is deducted as 1/4th deduction towards personal expenses, the annual dependency figure would come to Rs.9,32,908.20 (Rupees Nine Lakhs Thirty Two Thousand Nine Hundred Eight and Twenty paisa) only.
On this figure, only 40% (not 50%) can be added towards future prospect.

If this is done, the figure comes to Rs.9,32,908.20 + Rs.3,73,163.28 =
Rs.13,06,071.48 (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Six Thousand Seventy One and Forty Eight paisa) only.

As the deceased was aged 38 years, by using the multiplier of 15, the figure then comes to Rs.1,95,91,072/- (Rupees One Crore Ninety Five Lakhs Ninety One Thousand and Seventy Two)
only.
Other permissible addition towards loss of consortium, funeral expenses, loss of love and affection and loss of estate, would not require a second look.
9. With the above computation, the compensation receivable by the claimants is quantified at Rs.1,98,05,072/- (Rupees One Crore Ninety Eight Lakhs Five Thousand and Seventy Two) only.
The interest @6% per annum is left undisturbed.

10. In terms of this Courts order (dated 16.09.2022), the insurance company had deposited before the MACT, the sum awarded by the MACT i.e., Rs.2,32,28,912/- (Rupees Two Crores Thirty Two Lakhs Twenty Eight Thousand Nine Hundred and Twelve) only.

As we have reached a lesser figure of Rs.1,98,05,072/- (Rupees One Crore Ninety Eight Lakhs Five Thousand and Seventy Two) only,
this sum with 6% interest from the application date, should be remitted to the claimants immediately.
The balance amount is permitted to be received back by the appellant  insurance company.
11. With the above, the matter stands disposed of.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
DECEMBER 11, 2024.
